item.title: Blind Amnesia
item.description: The more time that passes, the more the good gets highlighted, and the bad fades into nothingness.
item.content:encoded:
I’m missing my ex today. It’s been almost exactly 2 months, and I guess things hit harder on milestones. The more time that passes, the more the good gets highlighted, and the bad fades into nothingness.

It was my choice to walk away. Our arguments were becoming more frequent, and instead of seeing growth in how we resolved things, I saw decline. I became increasingly frustrated at how long it took for the smallest issues to get resolved. It was in that frustration that I began to realise I was becoming someone I did not want to be.

Dealing with the passing of my dad had a big effect on it all. I was letting myself go. I stopped exercise and I wasn’t eating much. But I couldn’t manage to pull myself together because every time I found the smallest amount of motivation or happiness an argument would erupt and pull me back down.

I knew that I had to walk away, but I still loved her. It’s a cruel thing, love, in many ways. How we love what is not good for us. How we spend so much time hoping that things will improve despite all evidence to the contrary.

I finally found the courage to leave. And life did get better. For me, it almost always does after a breakup. I tend to use the time to focus inward, to find myself again, and to return to who I am. And that’s exactly what happened this time. I got back to being me.

Without the regular arguments, my free time was filled with peace and silence. All year I had needed that, and finally it was here. There was now a space for me to feel and to begin truly healing the wounds that my dad’s passing had left behind.

Still, I long for the good times. The happiness in imagining a future together. The warm cuddles and comforting laughs. No relationship is all bad, and walking away leaves you missing what had been good all along.

I catch myself in moments as I notice the blind amnesia. The focus on only what was good. I forget that I had lost myself; I forget that I had been lacking the room to breathe, and I forget that I was not able to show up authentically in my grief.

I’m having one of those moments right now as I write this. Looking back on old photos, following old chains of thought. Questioning my decisions. There is a sadness, but behind it, logic still rules. I did what was best for me. At least for now.

item.title: The Sting of Silence
item.description: A reflection on the pros and cons of the now traditional dopamine hits provided by online platforms.
item.content:encoded:
Since putting my writing back online I have noticed an odd silence. This site is static, and it has no integrated feedback loop. It has made me realise that I have grown accustomed to the reactions and comments provided by modern platforms.

Identifying a Conflict

My workflow has been to create, then upload, then obsessively check the reactions. And if my art performed poorly, it would affect my emotional state. Making me want to quit, or worse still, hide away.

Publishing something here leaves me with no feedback, no little hearts of recognition, no comments to satisfy or destroy my ego. Just silence. The act of posting completes the work of creation.

Its oddly satisfying, almost like sitting alone at the beach listening to the waves roll in. Or rolling up the tent door from a mountain top to witness the birds dancing at sunrise.

Attention Cravings

Even so part of me craves that feedback loop. I want to know if people are seeing me. I want to know what they think about what I have to say. I find the option of accepting feedback practical. It helps to improve and to motivate.

Although, if I am being honest, those wants also assume that feedback is positive.

Silent Relief

A different part of me finds relief in the silence. The opinions of others have no control over the value I place on my art. I can create freely. I can love the process, and I can love the results. Then I can release it, no feedback, no outside influence to affect my emotional stability. Only my opinion and my happiness for having created something.

I find posting into silence romantic and freeing. It lets me create as if in private while still sharing a piece of me with an unknown and possibly non-existent audience. Instead of holding the work open for reaction, it marks the end of the creation process. The posting becomes an act of release.

So What Now

As I write this, I am trying to decide which of these two paths will serve me better long term. Should I implement reactions and comments or should I embrace the silence?

I don’t have the answer today. So for now I will do nothing and continue to relish the space that comes after hitting upload.

item.title: Running Toward the Light
item.description: A raw look at how I'm turning the hardest year of my life into a reason to keep pushing forward.
item.content:encoded:
The Weight of it All

First, let me fill you in on the current situation.

I’m based in Valencia, Spain. Recently single, going through the hardest year of my life.

Its not only that my relationship ended, or that I got caught up being an unexpected dad to 5 guinea pigs.

Its not only that I lost my dad right before New Years, or that the funeral preparations were an absolute disaster full of opportunists, or that the circumstances around his death were extremely suspicious.

Its not only that my sister decided to stop speaking to me during all of this, or that I stopped eating and lost 10kg of muscle.

Its not only that my one best friend left the city, or that my savings are running low, or that AI has shaken up my career landscape.

But the worst of it all is that I lost my confidence and my own mind turned against me. For a while anyway.

Putting Up a Fight

The more life beat me, the less effect it seemed to have. I began to realise that at the end of all of this I too would end up taking the long cold nap and nothing that happened today was really as serious as that.

And my dad always told me:

“Never give up”

So I summoned what was left inside of me and started to dig my way back out.

Hitting the Pavement

I got back into running and found a release from the stress.

I often hoped a day would come that I would spend mornings running on the beach with my dad. That day never came. Yet despite him being gone I feel him running with me now, even though he hated running.

In the last 18 weeks I went from the couch to my first half marathon. And now I’ve started training for my first full one. I’m at 26 of 42 km so far.

Sunrises and Sea Water

I’ve also been running a community with some friends that meets every Tuesday to watch the sunrise from the ocean water.

I can’t say its been easy, many Tuesday mornings I wished I could avoid it. But I’m happy I didn’t, it’s kept me at least a little sane through this absolute ringer of a year.

Connecting with Something Greater

I found God again, or perhaps God found me. Not in the traditional religious sense. I don’t find myself aligning with Christianity, or Catholicism, or Islam. I just feel connected with this idea that there is something greater and grander than what we are. Something that many call God, but then go on to define in different ways.

I’ve been talking to Him. Very relaxed like, as if speaking with an old friend, and it’s been helping me. I also talk to my dad. Both are one way conversations.

Building an Escape Hatch

I’ve been putting in work to grow on social media, rather unsuccessfully I might add. Most days I consider quitting, but then I remind myself of the internal growth that showing up has given me.

Facing the embarrassment of failing in public, and accepting the sting of working on something you are proud of. Only for it to receive no recognition.

Its been a whirlwind of an adventure. From not caring, to caring, to caring too much, to realising its only ever been about creating to being with.

One Step in Front of the Other

For the most part, life is a mixture of hope and fear. Hope, for the positive change that I can see in the light at the end of this tunnel. Fear, for the possibility that I am wrong about that light and it just turns out to be more darkness.

Regardless I carry on daily. Because I have come to realise that when you don’t know what to do just put one foot in front of the other and hope that your legs take you to a better place.

The Path Forward

During this process I stumbled across my old writings. Blogs, short stories, and poems. All outlets that I used to value once upon a time.

After reading and feeling the past through them I’ve decided to return to the world of pen to paper, or finger to key. And as testimony to that, this is my first addition to my new collection of writings. Because even if nobody ever reads this, I may stumble across it in the future and remember what it was like to be here today.

And be thankful that I made it through it all.

item.title: Be Grateful for the Challenges
item.content:encoded: I have had a very interesting last 3 months. It has become clear that I have not been making the best decisions in my life and I am now left dealing with the repercussions of these choices. My biggest challenge of late has been trying to get myself balanced. I regularly find myself challenged and the thought crosses my mind to give up and to move towards the victim mentality. It was a little bit of a coping mechanism in the past and the challenge is now to break the habit. I am pushing myself to be grateful for the things that I do have, as well as reminding myself that even without anything just being alive is a blessing. Life comes with many experiences, some good, some bad, but none of which you could experience if you were not alive. I have plans for the future, I have some ideas and I am taking steps to reach them. The path is not clear as of yet, but I am working on it everyday and trying to ensure that my decisions are leading me where I intend to go. I remember thinking in a past moment that it would be interesting to see where life will be taking me. I find myself thinking the same again, as though I have finally awoken from a long nap and I am now ready to take action. One thing I have noticed is that the hard times in my life tend to attract me towards comfort. The more stress I am experiencing the more I want to indulge in things that I normally would believe to not be great for me. It is a fine line that we walk in this life, and it seems that at any moment we could vere off into another direction. For this reason I remain diligent and hopeful of the future.

item.title: I Have a Life
item.content:encoded: It’s a strange thing looking back at days past. I’ve been going through my old photos clearing up the ones that mean nothing in an attempt to create an album that I will actually use. Some memories are good and make me happy, but others bring sadness. People I have lost, people who are still alive but we no longer speak. Some of them we just lost contact because of time, others hearts I broke, or perhaps my drunken behaviour forced them to leave. I know that I can never go back, that changing the past is not possible and the only step forward is to learn from it. The sadness and pain of longing makes me crave a cigarette, or some beer. Anything to take away the feeling that hits me at this moment. How I would love to share my love with those that used to exist in my life in days past. I hope that one day we meet again, in a new world with forgiveness in our hearts ready to start a new. I miss you all.

item.title: Sunrise/Sunset
item.content:encoded:
It’s a funny thing life. The consistency of the battle that is. It seems that no matter what I do to get myself back up, I eventually find myself down again. Down and questioning but what is the point. But are we asking ourselves the right questions?

Is there truly a point to life. Inevitably we are all going to leave this plane of existence, one way or another depending on your beliefs. Nothing we collect in this life will come with us, perhaps not even our memories and experiences. Its as if our entire existence will be wiped clean on our deathbeds, or at the very least once the last person on earth remembers our name.

If we cannot control this common fact, what can we control? Perhaps only the years in between. The dash on your gravestone. Surely we have control over this. However, many of us find ourselves continuing to live an existence that does not fulfill us. Doing things purely to help the clock tick, living as if we will live forever.

What would over lives mean if we seized every opportunity, lived every moment, smiled at every stranger. What unbelievable tap would we open, what abundance would come pouring into our lives.

For just 1 week witness the sunrise and the sunset everyday and see how it changes you!

item.title: Commiting to the Grind
item.content:encoded: I have been slowly finding my way again. Step by step, brick by brick, moving forward, building myself up. It is hard to explain how good it feels to be on the right track, one thousand times or more better than over indulging as I did before. It’s more difficult that’s for sure. I find myself reading labels again and with less choices in my purchases since changing to eating plant based. Waking up at 6am can be tough but not nearly as tough as going to bed at 22:00. Step by step, brick by brick. I am growing and proud to be improving. I will grind until the day I die, I will be the best version of me possible.

item.title: Relationship Patterns
item.content:encoded:
Here I am, coming out of my second relationship in 8 months. I jumped straight from one into another and followed the same patterns. It’s clear to me that I need to do some serious work on myself before I undertake another one. I did some research and I am showing signs of emotional immaturity. So here it goes. Here are the things you should watch out for next time you enter a relationship.

  1. Don’t fall to early, give the relationship time to grow. Chances are if you fall to early it’s not real attraction but the fulfillment of some unfulfilled need.
  2. Don’t break up too soon. Relationships are hard work. If you want to break up every time things get hard, then your not ready to be in one.
  3. Don’t be needy. A healthy person realises that everyone needs their space. Make sure not to demand too much time. Be available not demanding.
  4. Make arguments productive. If an argument is not going to be productive there is really no need to have it, and if you have many unproductive arguments it might be time to look inward. It takes two to argue.

So today I am starting fresh. The rebirth of Kalen Michael. It’s difficult for me to look back at the last year and how far I fell from my ideal self. At the time it seemed like I would never fall this low again. Yet here I am, making the same mistakes, living the same poor lifestyle choices. It’s ironic. But today it changes. Today I am starting fresh, the new me will become what the old me once was, only better. I woke up at 6am and went for a run, then I had a meditation session. At 9am I will head out to meet Alan, my business partner, so we can make some sales. Today I get back on track, I am going to forget about women for awhile until I am strong enough to be who I need to be.

item.title: Like a Moth to the Flame
item.content:encoded:
Recently I have fallen short of my goals. My to do lists vanished for about a month and I found myself doing much less than normal. My exercise routine dropped to once per week, yoga became erratic, and I haven’t read much in the last month. Depression was closely shadowing me, and whether the lack of goalkeeping was causing the depression or the depression was causing the lack of goalkeeping, I found myself achieving less than expected. My diet suffered too as meals became less regular and I ate out more often.

I spent the last 3 days in bed recovering from a cold which gave me time to think and internalise something. This has given me the courage to begin building myself back up to where I was two months ago. This entry is to serve as a reminder that sometimes we fall down, but we can always get back up again!

item.title: I Find my Passion
item.content:encoded:
Recently I have felt uneasy about the goals I set myself some months ago. I decided that it was time to consolidate the goals I have set into my life long purpose. It is possible this will change over the coming months, years, or decades. Yet with this new purpose I feel at ease.

“I want for nothing. Everything I need and want is made available for me at the right moment. In every situation, I offer the best of myself. I give my best of me to everyone I meet. Guided by meditation and self-discovery I give through my heart, my soul and my passion. Everyday and in everyway, I work towards my goals. I never give up. I connect people. I help them to express their inner identities by shining a light on the goodness. I remind people of their inner beauty and of their potential, in the process, I discovered my own. I train the Mind and the Body. Mind is improved through meditation, reading, affirmations and correct mindset. Body is improved through healthy vegan nutrition, calisthenics and yoga. Body and Mind are jointly trained with cold showers, minimalism, and no fap. I live a life of love and compassion. I am love. And so it is!”

item.title: My World Gets Darker
item.content:encoded:
Momentum has slowed down and what was easy is beginning to seem a little more difficult. My iron will power has begun to chip and it shows signs of being hollow. I question myself what could be bringing this about. I sleep more, much more. Unaware whether I am tired or whether I am escaping a short rest turns into a several hour sleep. I remind myself of the cycle of my life.

Could it be my diet that is causing these changes as it has definitely begun to falter. Perhaps it is the mental changes as my brain begins to consolidate the ideas of religion into my ones agnostic paradigms. I try not to cling and remind myself that this too will pass.

item.title: Spiritual Path
item.content:encoded:
I find myself in an interesting position. It has been many years since I have considered devotion to a God. I have been agnostic and even vengeful to the idea of a God. My mind is tangled with confusion as it attempts to understand what it happening. My quest for worldly fulfillment has brought me full course back to spirituality. I find many ideas easy to accept as my Self-Development journey express many of the same concepts. Could it be that spirituality is the glue that holds it all together?

I do not feel this to be a passing fad. It is becoming clear that I am being called to religion, to spirituality, to God. With each passing moment I can feel the pull becoming stronger along with my desire to dedicate myself to a life of study and meditation. My struggle is in connecting my worldly ambitions with those of the divine.

It will be interesting to watch as this path unfolds, the discovery is thrilling. Who will I be at the next intersection of my life? The question both excites and scares me. This is a profound change in my beliefs and attitudes. This will surely redirect the course of my life. I find myself praying to the Divine Mother for guidance, an act I would not have even entertained in the not so distant past. “Free me from the illusion of this life, do with me as you will.”

item.title: Strange Occurences
item.content:encoded:
I find myself in an interesting place at the moment. With my recent efforts towards self-improvement and realisation I had begun to neglect my meditation. Seeking to replace it with the time spent in Yoga and Pranayama. I completed my first round of chosen guide books which I had categorised as follows: The 4 hour workweek by Tim Ferris - Freedom Think and Grow Rich by Napoleon Hill - Wealth How to Win Friends and Influence People by Dale Carnegie - Relationships Psycho-Cybernetics by Max Maxwell - Mindset At the time of completion I did not think much of this and decided to read an unrelated book before starting my second round. While eating lunch, I was waiting for a YouTube video to load and an advert appeared that introduced me to Autobiography of a Yogi by Yogananda. The advert had such an effect on me that I began to investigate more about the book. On discovering that many prominent people had read this book, some many times, I decided to consider buying it. Find the book for £1.50 I promptly purchased it.

I have been deeply drawn to the book and reading it has been very easy even passing around two hours the second day of reading. Strangely I began to feel that this book should be added to my reading round as the Spiritual book. I imagined that it was the glue that held the others together. Interestingly there are many ideas that are shared with the other books of my reading round.

When the Vedic was mentioned I recalled my earlier friend explaining his vedic astrology to me. At the time I didn’t listen much as I found astrology to be a topic not worth my time. This book sparked my interest and I decided to get my chart done. After reading my chart I felt devoid of energy and took a long nap. When I eventually woke up I was urged to continue reading the book which began promptly by explaining astrology and our ability to change what was written.

I am unsure what road I am being taken down but I believe myself to be in the right place.

item.title: Embracing Life
item.content:encoded:
Following the advice of Psycho-Cybernetics I did some mind clearing and visualization exercises before work yesterday and hit my highest sales numbers. It really works. I feel great today, truly ecstatic.

The daily work I have been putting in, the grinding, is starting to show its fruit. My boss even told me that she wants me to be her right hand man!

So a gentle reminder, when the going gets tough, when it seems like you are working for nothing, keep going! You cannot see the benefits day by day but over the long term the results are dramatic. You are working towards your future one way or another, either create the future you want or let it be created for you.

Give your best, everyday, in every way, and never give up.

item.title: Regaining Focus
item.content:encoded:
At times in life we can get so caught up in trying to achieve something that we completely lose track of the reason we started in the first place. We work so hard at something day by day that we begin to believe it is what we are working on that is necessary. It almost comes to define us.

For that reason I believe we should, at regular intervals, stop and review our lifestyle choices and inspect whether we are in fact heading in the right direction.

Fitness
To become stronger and more able. To move freely without restriction. To feel energized and alive. I use these activities to accomplish this: calisthenics, yoga, and dance.

Health
To be healthy. To not experience undue pain. To operate at an optimal level. For this I eat a whole food diet 95% of the time. I also practice Pranayama.

Money
To have enough money that it no longer becomes a concern. To free my mind to think about other things than money. To free my time to concentrate on what is important to me regardless of how much it pays. I am building a brand to accomplish this.

Intelligence/Mindset
To have a mind that promotes positive actions. To find the good in all situations. To never limit myself due to incorrect thoughts. To find new ways to grow. For this I read self-help books and practice affirmations.

Spirituality
To be at peace with the Earth. To feel compassion and love for all things. To not allow myself to feel insignificant or to belittle others. I practice gratitude writing, Buddhism and veganism.

Skills
To acquire useful skills that aid me on my journey. To build confidence in myself and my abilities. To feel as though I have the tools needed to live the life I want. I practice the bo-staff, speaking from my diaphragm, selling successfully, and correct posture.

For all things in life have a reason and a purpose. Yet to lose sight of this is a great loss indeed. How can one pursue their dreams when they lack the direction they are meant to proceed.

item.title: When Easy Becomes Hard
item.content:encoded:
I’m approaching two months in Madrid. It’s been an interesting experience and I have come much further than I thought I would. I remember sitting in Turks and Caicos thinking I would never make it here in Spain. Focusing on all the potential things that would go wrong.

What’s strange is that my attitude has now shifted and now I find myself without any desire to return. I look back on my time in the Caribbean with an overall distaste. Despite all the beauty, it offered and the rescue from loneliness I was becoming someone other than me.

It took the spontaneous commitment to leave to turn that around. I felt myself returning almost as soon as I landed in Madrid airport. My first few weeks were spent very much idly hoping for the best. I took some action towards finding work and maintaining my mood. Yet mostly I just socialised and experienced my time in Spain.

Slowly the momentum built up and I found myself exercising daily and focusing more on my goals. After finding work and a room to rent the stability ensured I could focus more on self-improvement. I committed myself to read, practice yoga and meditate. These three activities became part of my morning routine and I did them as soon as I woke up every day. It was easy. Along with these I continued to exercise daily and only seemed to slack off on the occasional leg day. Leg workouts do not really excite me much, it is the exercises themselves that do not offer much in the way of excitement.

Over time the new and exciting exercises became normal and habit’s formed. Unfortunately with this came complacency. It became easier to take days off. This was the usual occurrence in my life. I would push myself hard for a period of time only to slowly revert to how things were before.

Not this time. This time I accept the challenge. Is it harder to continue?! At the moment, yes, I find it more difficult to stick to my goals. Yet that will not prevent me from giving it all I have. I will continue to push forward with the challenges I have set for myself.

I wanted to record this event as this is the exact moment in time I would normally give up. I would feel that I deserve a break and that break would become permanent. I have done this countless times in my life and I refuse to continue repeating the same life over and over again.

Today I declare that easy has become hard, and that hard will not break me. I will keep pushing on. I will keep working hard. I will succeed in my endeavours for I am the protagonist of my story. I create the life I want.

Often when we find something becoming difficult it is because we have forgotten to break down the task into smaller segments. Chunking is the way forward. It only takes one step to start a journey and another one step continues the very same.

I will conquer this challenge. Whether it takes me a day or a lifetime!

item.title: Lost, How to Find Your Way
item.content:encoded:
Sometimes in life we find ourselves unsure of the next best step. Heck sometimes we don’t even know what to do next, let alone what is best. Plan as you may, sometimes life will blindside you. You are going to wake up at some point and be completely clueless about your direction.

When this happens. When you find yourself staring down a long empty road entirely unsure of what to do next. Remember “shit happens”.

Progress is not a straight line, instead it comes in intervals. In between every improvement you spend a lot of time just being mediocre. Grinding. All the best things in life come from hard work. Boring work. Waking up early work. Blood, sweat and tears, work. It’s never too late to start putting in the work. Just remind yourself what it is you are striving for. And when times get hard, when you get lost. When there is no clear way forward. When you are lost in the jungle. When the waves are threatening to sink your ship. When no one is hearing you cry. When you are abandoned. When the world seems empty and you seem lost. That’s when it really counts. Everything before was practice, now you are in the game. This is when the moment calls to prove what you have. Prove what you can do. It’s always tougher, always harder when it counts. Practice is preparation. Game time is game time. Will you break or will you make it?

So, what do you do when you have no idea what to do? List your choices, compare them with your ultimate goals and then choose the one that fits best. You only get one choice. Then do that, with everything you have, no matter how hard it feels. Push harder. Get yours.

item.title: Money is Tight: Stretching whats left to Buy Time
item.description: I'm established but not yet stable, its going to take a little more work to make this sustainable.
item.content:encoded:
Spanish music plays silently in the background as I gaze out of the third floor window. Desert plants decorate the window sill and bring a sense of comfort. The room is painted in an Autumn style. Almost ironic as I look out into Summer.

Time is Flying By

In a few days I will have been in this bustling city for three weeks. The first week felt like it took a month to pass yet the following two passed as quickly as a meteor in the night sky. The rich culture and foreign language captivated the senses.

It was easy to be at peace in this moment, I had come far since arriving in Spain. With a backpack, €600, and a credit card already €800 in debt I started my adventure. I always knew that I was spending more than I had. Throughout my life I have not allowed myself to get into debt with financial institutions, opting rather to pay off any borrowed money before the interest set in. Yet I had been practicing daily to let go of these thoughts. To remain at peace despite my worries.

This time around it was not a luxury I could afford. I needed the cash to secure a rented room. And I would need to keep using the credit card until such time as my incomings surpassed my outgoings.

The Over Spender

I suppose I could have been more careful to start. Perhaps I ate out more often than I needed to. It was my first hostel accommodation that made budgeting difficult. The hostel was clean, safe, and warm. It offered most of what I needed. In fact it was this hostel that helped me to secure my first job, taking travelers out to eat Tapas. A traditional Spanish snack that is usually served alongside alcohol. The challenge at the time was the missing kitchen. Without a kitchen most of my meals were from restaurants. The vibrant vegan community in Madrid meant that I was not short of options. Having spent 3 months on a small island with little change, the diversity had my mouth watering.

When I eventually moved myself into a cheaper hostel and one that included a kitchen. I found that I could spend €4 for 5 days. This made a huge impact on my budgeting. I always remind myself not to look back, yet it’s hard not to see the savings I could have made from moving here first. Everything happens for a reason.

The difficulty of hostel life is that you find yourself never alone. 24 hours 7 days a week you have people around you. Your isolation mostly includes time in the bathroom. Even then there is always noise reminding you that you are not alone. The smells make sleeping interesting and there is always someone coming or going. Your sleep is never solid and you end up waking up several times throughout the night, every night.

Yet despite these challenges, it is humbling to have little more than a rented bed and a locker. Part unpacking and packing everyday. The truth of it is that in comparison to my 3 months cycling Western Europe this was luxury. Even the cold shower was better than no shower at all. I often find myself amazed at how little we really need. Once we lay down roots we begin to accumulate so many things and we truly believe we need them all. When you wake up with nothing more than what you can carry you feel truly free and you begin to question the origin of your thoughts before.

After three weeks I find myself here, finally alone. I managed to secure a rented room and with my part time work I am only making a loss of €65 per week.

I never really find myself feeling at home. At least in the traditional sense of settling down. I have however always loved Spain and the opportunity to pass some time here truly excites me.

The song on the radio changes and I’m back here in the present. One deep breathe follows the next. Happiness is truly a choice.

item.title: Fear and Confidence
item.description: Relfections on fear.
item.content:encoded:
Confidence building. The art of becoming confident. It’s a funny thing to consider. In fact, most of us do not believe we are good enough. Even the vast majority of those who will say they do believe it are still held back by various limiting beliefs:

  • The fear of missing out.
  • The fear of not being good enough.
  • The fear of approaching someone they find attractive.
  • The fear of being laughed at.
  • The fear of being judged.

I once heard it said that:

“Fear is an acronym for False Evidence Appearing Real.”

In many ways this makes sense. If you think about it, fear always comes before anything bad actually happens. And before something happens there is always an equal and just as likely opportunity that something good will happen.

Ask yourself why do we always assume the worst? If it is our evolutionary tact. A survival mechanism that keeps us from perishing and if so does it also keep us from truly living? I wonder how long it would take to begin truly replacing fear with confidence. To make the first thought that enters our brains a good one.

To truly wish ourselves the best in every day and moment!

item.title: Settling In: The Beginnings of a New Life Start to Emerge
item.description: Life is getting established and its starting to feel a little more like a home.
item.content:encoded:
Waking up to chirping birds has become a regular occurrence. Occasionally the clashing of a glass in the distance meets the strum of a Spanish guitar, signaling the start of the day. It is always hot and for that my window remains open. I’m reminded that this is Spain.

I’m filled with a sense of pride when I think back on the few weeks I’ve been here.

Speaking in Foreign Tongues

Despite having traveled and even relocated many times, this is the first time I’ve attempted to settle somewhere where I cannot rely on my English. The 5 months I spent traveling through Spain in 2012 give me an obvious advantage. Even though my grammar needs some serious work, I am able to communicate. Sometimes I forget I’m not speaking my mother tongue.

Its a Trendy City

I find Madrid to be a fascinating city and I am particularly enamored with Retiro park. Drawn there on a daily basis to join in the athletic displays on the local calisthenic bars. Between sets, I find it exhilarating to watch the locals skateboard, roller-blade and even cycle backwards around the fountain in front of me.

The years I spent in London conditioned me to have a certain opinion of cities, an opinion which is quickly being shattered by the Spanish capital. Rather than the cosmopolitan display of suits and high fashion I find this city filled with trendy youth covered in tattoos and sporting interesting and unusual hairstyles. Perhaps I fit in here, walking around, Spotify blasting away on my headphones, it does feel like home.

Interesting Characters

In the weeks leading up to today, I managed to secure work, a place to live and navigate the confusing Spanish bureaucracy to obtain temporary legal status. I have been blessed to meet many amazing people. While many often move on to Barcelona, San Sebastián or even back towards their homes, I am truly grateful to have shared in their lives for just a moment.

Rohan, the friendly Indian who welcomed me on my first day in Madrid, embarked on his journey to share with his mother that he had been living a double life and was in-fact gay. He confided in me the irrational fear that arises from living in a country that does not allow people to be themselves. When he messaged me to say he was leaving Spain and his mother took the news well, I felt my heart skip a beat. For that short moment, I could share in his happiness. He could now be himself, if nowhere else at least at home.

Izabela, emancipated herself at 16, not because of family problems but because she craved independence and that paired with her intelligence enabled her to start university at that young age. Despite being only 21 as she sits across the table from me, I sense an old soul. With wisdom and compassion, she quotes many masters and shares her experiences traveling the world. She provides me with faith, faith that humanity can do better, that we can be better.

These are only two of the awe-inspiring characters I have met. Each unique individual inspiring me in some small way to be grateful for what I have, to fight for what I want and to never give up.

Feeling Thankful

This beautiful city, these wonderful people, they give me pride in my existence and I remain humble in this honour. How I wish I could share the blessings of this life with everyone I hold dear.

For now, know that I hold you all in my heart with me.

item.title: Taking it Personally, Advice to a Sister
item.content:encoded:
A friend recently mentioned to me a problem she was facing. A friend of hers had pointed out a fault she was being bothered by and did so in a way that was hurtful. Her friend had mentioned that it had been discussed when she was not around. This left her feeling as though her friends were against her and left her doubting the value of her friendships. She was also worrying about who may have been involved in this talking behind her back. Perhaps you have found yourself in a similar situation?

The first thing I constantly remind myself is: What people say about me when I’m not around is NONE OF MY BUSINESS! Don’t get caught up in gossip, even if that gossip involves you. Everyone is entitled to their own personal views. Often people will talk about something or someone only to vent the issue and in doing so perhaps realize it was not as extreme as they had originally thought. If the matter is serious they will bring it up to you in time. Although those around you the freedom to express their emotions without being offended. Even if the topic is sometimes you.

If an issue is eventually raised to you remember this: A constructive criticism is not a criticism of you as a person but a small action or habit you have. Do not make a mountain out of a molehill. We often add our own baggage to the words of others completely distorting the meaning and intentions.

Take it at face value! A door is a door and a window is a window. Stop telling yourself stories!!

item.title: A Beach Day
item.content:encoded:
Reflected on the white sand were shimmers of light caused by the light movement of the water above. Perhaps it was the waters’ way of expressing the stars it had seen the night before. The water was so clear it was easy to see right to the bottom. The tiny fish that swam in large groups cast inch long shadows. Creating a depth not easy to imagine and yet so hard to forget.

The waves in the distant though calm lapped a starfish ashore. Unsure of its intention I returned this tropical creature to the sea. There was magic in the air and I did all I could to swallow the images with my eyes.

If perfection was a moment this would be it. Behind me just off the beach was a single tree that cast a shadow, a shelter from the sunlight. Underneath it sat my father, my stepmother, their dog who had inherited the role of my sister and the woman I had come to love in the recent weeks.

When we all got up to walk it was through the knee-high water. I pushed our dreaded dog along on the paddle board. It felt to me like we were voyagers, adventurers on an exciting discovery. And in some ways we were. We entered a secluded cove that had a natural beach. Above the water carved cave, we found the carvings of pirates that had been before, yet were now long gone.

item.title: Leaving Home: Starting Over for the Third Time
item.description: Navigating the emotional turbulence of leaving home and stepping back into the unknown.
item.content:encoded:
Except for the two airport personnel, security was empty. Not something I usually experienced on international flights. After the usual undress and pat down I found myself in the departure terminal. Smaller than usual it was just what you would expect from such a small island.

This was it I was one step closer to leaving the place I called home for the last 3 months. It was a short time but it was with my dad and that made it home.

The Waiting Game

I identified the gate and put on some music. The intention was to drown out the thinking that inevitably occurs when you leave loved ones behind. But even distractions can only hold you for so long. The flight was delayed for unknown reasons and I eventually grew tired of the pacing and head bobbing. I retired to a chair. We finally began the boarding process and I found the music no longer offered me solace.

As the longing and reminiscing began it occurred to me that I had not yet left the island. Sitting in the plane I could see the small hills and fences that separated those leaving from those staying. Only a mere 10 minutes drive away was everything I now missed.

Take off took us over the roads I had been driving on and then over the areas I had worked and played. I held back the tears by reminding myself to look forward and not back. I could not undo the past but if the absence of this place, of these people, became unbearable I could always return.

Reflecting on Paradise

This island, this beautiful blue sea. I have been blessed to spend so much time in such an awe inspiring place. Surely I would find myself here again. As the memories flooded my mind I found myself battling the fear of the unknown, and perhaps the fear of missing out.

This was it, this was life. I’m sure one day I would look back at this very moment and find it to be an interesting story. Maybe it would teach me some life changing lessons or maybe I would just laugh at my naivety. For surely this was just a temporary trip away, like leaving home to buy bread only to return with more than you had when you left.

Growth and Characters

My time on paradise had taught me much. My flaws that had been pointed out and carved into my mind were now paths towards improvement. Unbelievable characters had introduced themselves. At times I felt like I was living in a ‘novella’. A short story about the island life and how you can choose to turn any situation into a blessing or a nightmare.

If grateful was a strong enough word I would use it. Yet it is found lacking in my appreciation for what has come my way in the recent months. And I only hope that I was worthy to receive such blessings.

Looking Forward

So out into the world I fly, crossing oceans, changing time zones and experiencing new cultures. In my heart, believing that once again those wonderful characters will make an appearance. And hopefully when they do, I will be able to give them back what they have given me, and then some.

item.title: The Bittersweet Caribbean Ending
item.description: Preparing to leave behind family once again and head into the unknown.
item.content:encoded:
The visions shared for the last 2.5 months evaporate instantly and in their place I see a sudden shift in colors. A single bed lies in front of me, a strange bed. The size and shape look new to me.

Feelings begin to rise up bringing pain of the looming departure. I find myself unsure whether I have been here before despite this being the very same bed I have been using my whole stay.

In this moment it all becomes clear to me. Sounds are louder, colors are brighter and my heart holds within it a light pain. The kind of pain you feel just before an untimely breakup. Or just before you part from those you love dearly unsure when you will once again share in each other’s spirit.

It’s a strange thing that the very fact that something can, or even will end, is what makes you wish it won’t.

item.title: Potential to Waste
item.description: A short story about inert objects, pondering how unfulfilled potential slowly fades into nothingness.
item.content:encoded:
Despite the usual warmth emitted from deep brown mahogany, the table glared a coldness I had not seen before from wood. It was as though it was still alive and reflected its feelings of isolation.

Resting in the middle of the table was a shiny silver pen. Its tip flared out and sharpened to a point like an unusual arrowhead. It lay there alone and no inkwell was in sight. While it had the ability to make a mark on the world, it could not do so without the ink it required. More importantly the pen depended upon someone to shape its movements and design its markings.

Directly below was a crisp white rectangle of paper. If you focused your eyes it was easy to make out the shallow depressions as the light danced around it. How would this paper complete its purpose without an animated object to mark it? As I looked at the scene in front of me it became clear that despite its potential nothing could change. One crucial ingredient had been missing. Without desire, action and movement these objects would lie here forever slowly decomposing. Until finally the potential they once showed no longer existed.

item.title: The Romance of the Stars
item.description: A quiet, midnight escape on a ruined roof, where a sudden spark and a starry sky turn an ordinary night into something unforgettable.
item.content:encoded:
Illuminating the sky was a crescent moon. It shone more white than yellow on this dark night. The moonlight, for the most part, was the only light around for miles. We looked up at the stars just off to the right, and in that instance I couldn’t help myself. I ran off to find a better view.

After placing an old ladder under the rafters of what appeared to be a hurricane damaged roof I fetched her. She looked so beautiful as I approached. Her long blonde hair reflected just enough light to contrast with the sky around her. Peering out into the night sky her presence made my heart skip a beat. Before I knew it, we were sitting on the rafters, then she was edging her way up the steep roof tiles. I joined her.

We lay there for what seemed like an eternity, sharing in our minds. We talked while the heavens blessed us and stars shot past us. Were I alone, I wouldn’t have braved climbing from the rafters onto the roof. It was when she confessed she wouldn’t have climbed the ladder to rafters without me that I knew. I knew then that I had found someone special and that together we would achieve anything.

item.title: Depression, a View from the Inside
item.description: What goes on inside the depressed mind of a troubled man.
item.content:encoded:
It all changed. Colours had drained and the future now seemed more distant and incoherent than it had ever been. The struggle is real and every simple action, every simple step now seems harder than climbing mount Everest. My brain is telling me that hunger is better than the effort required to make food. I want to cry but I cannot seem to muster enough sadness. I am sad, but it’s as though the sadness has gone beyond its point of origin and has replaced itself with a void. Feelings have no place here and emotions that should drive me to tears reveal themselves as a lump in my throat. I feel heavy tension in my forehead and cheekbones. I’m unable to relax my neck.

My inner voices do battle with each other. One strong voice silently whispers, “There is no point in carrying on. You have come as far as you need come. Die, extinguish yourself.” While another weak and distant voice screams for survival. It reminds me to carry on, that things will get better. The sun will shine and I will once again find happiness. If I just put in the work.

Then the authority stands up. The oldest voice of them all and it says, “That’s all well and good, but you know you will feel this way again. Life is always going to be a struggle. Why struggle. You can see clearly now. It’s time to end this game.”

I’m able to force myself to take some small action but it musters most of my will power. And after I feel more drained than when I began. I know that exercise will help, but exercise seems pointless. I know that eating well will improve my feelings, but preparing food seems too hard. I feel alone despite being around other people. They don’t understand, how could they.

They look at me and see laziness. But I have felt laziness and this is not the same. They look at me and see apathy. But I care, I care too much. Without the care I would be long gone. I would have played out one of my many fantasies. I would have swam out into the ocean until tiredness took me away. I would have climbed the tallest structure only to take the quick way down. I would have plunged a knife deep into my abdomen. But I care, I care too much, and I fear pain.

There was a time not so long ago where I felt I could conquer the world. Nothing would stop me from reaching for what I wanted. Now I fear that I no longer want anything. And if I did, I am no longer worthy to receive it.

The only rest seems to come from sleep, and the hope that I will not awaken. Inside I wish to scream, but I don’t know what I want to scream about. I want to cry but I have no tears. I want to die but I have no courage.

I have climbed the highest mountains only to dive into the lowest seas. It is not the beasts and monsters of the outside world that plague me. I am not prevented from reaching success by any outside force. Instead my world has turned against me. My mind has become my enemy.

The colours around me are no longer bright. My future seems bleak. And should I not find my light I fear the light shall not find me. As irrational as this all seems. It’s as real as the blood in my veins. Like a see saw I rock from wanting to live to wanting to die. In all this confusion I am able to discern that it is not death that I wish upon myself but rather the cessation of suffering.

And when all of life seems to bring more suffering how else do you set yourself free?

Today I will not die. Today I will not live. Today I merely exist waiting, waiting for it all to end.

item.title: Fatherly, a Poem
item.description: A reflection on the boring moments with my dad.
item.content:encoded:
Waking Early, Zombie Walks
Kitchen Refills, Work Drive Talks
Birds chirp faster, Cool wind blows
Sunlight showers, Darkness exposed

item.title: Day Seventy-Nine: Reaching Santiago, Rebirth at Cape Finisterre, and the Final Push to Lisbon
item.description: Completing the Camino de Santiago, performing a cleansing ritual on the edge of the Atlantic, and gearing up for the final stretch to Portugal.
item.content:encoded:
Day 65 – 68

This was the final push to complete my Camino de Santiago. My time on the way was spiritual and I enjoyed most of the cycle. In my early days, I had decided to treat this as a sort of rebirth. I would lay everything on the line as I headed towards the Compestella. This would be my final trek as the person I was. On finishing my journey I would be fresh and new. All my past mistakes would be forgiven. I reminded myself of this each time I faced a steep uphill when the rain soaked my socks or continuing on just seemed impossible.

I rode the 100 km into Santiago in one day. Despite this trip being spiritual to me, I was also happy for it to end so that a new chapter could begin. Collecting stamps were becoming particularly annoying. Many people enjoy this part of the Camino and end up keeping their passports as treasured keepsakes. With my minimalist mindset, I imagined it would not stay with me long after I had received my Compestella. A necessary evil I suppose.

Anit Climax. That’s how I would express the Compestella. Covered in scaffolding pictures were not really exciting. Even receiving my certificate didn’t offer me much satisfaction. By this point, the journey had given me so much more than either of the two former could ever offer. It’s funny that we pass by so much beauty in quest of this church, almost ironic.

I still wanted a decent conclusion and so I decided to head to Cape Finisterre. Many pilgrims continue there journey onto this point. It also holds the official o.oo km marker stone. I managed to get there just after sunset completing the 90 km in one day. It was great to be back near the ocean and the way there was a beautiful cycle.

To celebrate I spent three nights in a flash hotel. This was a milestone I didn’t want to go unnoticed. While to some this may have just been the end of a long trip. To me, this was my rebirth. From here on out I was a new person. I would dedicate myself to being the absolute best I could be. Every day until death.

I held a ceremony on a rock overhanging the ocean. Here I said some words and forgave myself for any of my undesirable past actions. I spoke a little about my past, and I made some pledges for my future. I announced loudly that I was now forgiven and reborn before washing myself in a deep rock pool. No one was around but the birds and the waves. This ceremony was for me, and me alone. I threw my burdens into the ocean and I hiked back up the cliff a lighter happier me.

Looking back at why I left London and started this cycle. I received what I was after and so much more!

Day 69 – 79

Now began the next leg of the trip. It was strange as my motives had now changed dramatically. I no longer wanted to live off the land, nor was I as excited about camping. Preferring to take the quicker routes than the quieter ones and reaching Lisbon was now my priority.

I mentally categorised this leg as the strengthening of my foundations. My focus now on building healthy habits and supportive thinking. I feel as though I have a sense of direction and purpose. At times it feels as though these final few kilometres are holding me back from accomplishing the things I want to achieve next. However, I am committed to completing the route to Lisbon. I made a promise to myself, and that I will never break.

I feel happy to spend the night in hostels and this has allowed me to meet some new interesting characters. Taking the time to understand them and their stories is helping me strengthen my own beliefs. We all walk such different paths, what is a weakness to one is a strength to another. When you stop judging yourself by other peoples success and failures it becomes easier to truly listen.

The road continues to throw up its challenges. I have faced a tire that keeps slipping off, a destroyed front hub, and I’m currently still sourcing a replacement rear wheel. It seems that the weight of my bags became too much for Zen and the damage to her rear wheel is irreparable. Ironically this is one of the most costly repairs I have needed to make and it comes 3 days before the finish line. But get there we must, and get there we will.

Surprisingly I feel little hesitation about arriving in Lisbon. Instead, I am excited to complete this stage and move onto my next one. While I will definitely be touring again, I now know undeniably that I want to keep some of my creature comforts. A walk on the wild side is a romantic getaway, but I am not willing to sacrifice modern luxuries indefinitely. I will, however, continue to live a more modest lifestyle.

So as soon as I am able to replace my rear wheel, which is currently on order at the local bike shop. I will be back on the road for my final three days of cycling before reaching Lisbon. After which I intend to hold some unforgettable celebrations. Another milestone and a heck of an achievement. Six months ago I could never have imagined myself completing something like this.

Whats after Lisbon? The intention is to sail to the Carribean. I will be working on the specifics once I’m a little more settled. The thought of a transatlantic crossing excites me and I think it is the next worthy goal.

item.title: Day Sixty-Four: They Call Me the Ice King
item.description: Blasting through snow-covered roads, surviving an exploding inner tube outside a gas station, and finding unexpected peace in a Galician monastery.
item.content:encoded:
There is life on the Camino after all. As I move closer to Santiago, the Compostela becomes more of a reality than a dream. I’m met by fellow pilgrims, more people than I have seen in all my days combined. Despite most of my route being isolated my dorm is now full. I find myself questioning whether it was, in fact, better on the lonesome road.

Before I enjoyed the silence of empty 60-bed dorms. I had an open reign in the hallways and common rooms became my garage. I’m now faced with limited space. Constant movement sounds as others struggle to find comfort in the well-used beds.

I had imagined that anyone I met on the Camino would be on a spiritual path. However, despite that we are all pilgrims there is a clear divide in the reasoning. It becomes apparent that there are many journeys being undertaken here. Not all of them are spiritual.

One woman has grown tired of the walking. Instead, she opts to take the bus from stage to stage. This turns what would be an 8-hour journey into 30 minutes. The reasoning seems to be so that she is still able to participate. Her friends continue stamping the road and enduring the endless hills without her. By the time the sun has set, they all eat dinner together as if the struggles of the day are equally shared.

I met a woman from Asturias. She has taken to the Camino to say goodbye to her beloved country. She is preparing to head to Romania for Erasmus. This final walk is the only way she could bear to leave her country behind.

There are those that make a habit of walking the Camino. The journey today is no more spiritual than the last one was. Some love the idea of collecting the stamps along the way. Then you have the silent ones, they speak little and don’t give away much. Only my imagination hints at the reasons behind there walk.

Watching has taught me not to ask why they walk. Instead, I wait for the information to be offered. The Camino is personal to some and I choose to respect that silent understanding. Some soul nourishing conversations were shared and friends have been made. No doubt I will see some of these people again. Yet I still find myself wishing for silence on occasion. I think back to early days when my thoughts alone accompanied me and I was the only pilgrim.

I hear rumours of the drunken celebrations happening near the Compostela. My vision of a peaceful holy place is replaced with busy pubs and drunken westerners. This strangles my desire to finish this Camino. I will however continue. Life has shown me to always form my own opinion. We all see life through a different lens.

Day 59

As I think back on what has happened over the last few days I find it difficult to find dividing lines. Each day has blended into the next. Mostly because I seemed to have experienced the same rainy weather, exhuasting long climbs, and similar mechanical failures day after day.

The focus of day 59 was to rebalance my rear wheel. I still needed the spoke tool to make this happen. Before I could start I needed to tend to a flat tire.

A smile formed on my face as I finally entered the bicycle shop which had been my destination for days. In broken Spanish and hand movements I signal my despair. “No tengo, vas a Navia para comprar” comes the response. He doesn’t have what I need. Its a further 16-kilometre ride to the next town.

I finally made it to Navia just before dark and got my hands on a spoke tool. Can you say amen! Riding with a wonky wheel is not only more difficult but it comes with along with the stress of further damage to other parts.

I spent the night indoors, it seemed easier.

Day 60

I woke up early to adjust my wheel and get everything balanced. It took some time and I could not do a perfect job. But it would have to do.

The day was wet with non-stop rain. Yet as I crossed a long bridge and left Asturias to enter Galicia the weather did not matter so much to me. Galicia had become a magical kingdom in my mind and I was looking forward to conquering the land.

Again I opted to stay indoors for the night. The excitement I had once felt for camping was waning in this wet and freezing weather. This gave me the opportunity to wash my dirty laundry, which now encompassed all the clothes I had.

Day 61 The day started with another flat tire; different wheel. I promised myself some better tires or puncture protectors at my next bicycle shop.

It was a testing day. It felt much more difficult to cycle. As I could not see any faults I assumed it must have been the hills or lack of energy from minimal sleep. When I spend the night indoors I end up staying up late to get some work done online. These are one of the only opportunities I have to use my laptop. The frequent McDonald’s stops I found in France does not seem to be as widely spread over here.

After a gruelling day of struggling up hills and braving the rain and freezing weather, a camp was a welcomed break. I found a covered woodland just off the main road. While it was unsuitable for a tent my hammock makes almost any terrain doable.

It was a quick pitch followed by a hurried meal. I then layered up and got into my sleeping bag. Warmth baby, that’s what I needed!

Day 62

Rain and hills. Snow and hills. Ok so it was beautiful and I definitely felt happy to be where I was. I mean who expects sunshine every day during winter (silly me).

Another flat! My hands now out of their comforting gloves are starting to freeze. Using the tools to change the inner tube is becoming difficult as a woman approaches me. Presumably to ask why I am in her driveway. I do my best to converse with her but her accent is strange. I am not able to make out much over the non-stop barking of her two large dogs. We stand for a moment in awkward silence before I get back to work.

I left really late today, it must have been around 13:30. The cold kept me wrapped up in my sleeping bag. The delay caused by the flat tire meant I couldn’t get really far.

Wet, cold and biting my tongue with anger slightly frustrated I stopped in a hostel for the night. This one had no hot water, but heating was all I really needed.

After dinner and some online work, I cleaned up my drivetrain. The difficulty riding turned out to be a binding chain. All the wet weather has washed out the lubrication from between the links. With all the challenges I hadn’t bothered to notice.

Day 63

I’m up early and determined to cover some distance. A more able cyclist could reach Santiago today. I’m happy to cover half the remaining distance. Something is driving me towards Sobrado dos Monxes.

The weather changes several times throughout the day. I see sunshine, rain, and snow. It’s hard to believe there was a time I had never touched snow. Now it seems to be a part of my daily routine. Snow is preferable to rain, its bounces off my waterproofs and I don’t get as wet. Plus the landscape is beautifully blanketed in white.

Heading down a steep hill at 45 kilometres a sudden pop spreads fear through my body. I slowly apply the brakes and careful head towards the side of the road. My rear inner tube has exploded?!

I want to get angry. I want to scream ‘Why me Lord?‘ Instead, I’m reminded of the Shaggy song and I smile. Just to my right, there is a gas station. Not only do I have a rain cover, I have an air pump. I also have a bucket to find a slow leak in my last remaining inner tube. To top it all off I have a sink and soap to clean up after the job. Now I’m more spiritual than religious, but really “Thank You, God!”.

It turns out that my rear tire had burst exposing the inner tube. These tires were old and I was expecting to replace them soon enough. I bought the bike second hand and then added another 2200 kilometres, I think they did well. I patch the tire with duct tape (this stuff is really handy!) and make my way to the closest bike shop.

The bike shop did all the work for me free of charge and I only paid for the parts. Conveniently they also improved the balance on my rear wheel and swapped out my brake pads. Then as I was leaving they gave me a free T-shirt. Oh yeah, Galician hospitality. #lovinglife

When I finally get where I am going I find the most beautiful monastery and it becomes home for the night. It’s not empty as expected but there are other pilgrims.

Day 64

Heavy snow today has me requesting an extra day from the monk in charge. He happily agrees. The day is spent with fellow pilgrims, some online work, and photography.

For a moment I find myself questioning what could make this moment better. I realise I am truly content, I don’t need anything else. Thinking back to my days in London, when I felt helpless. In those days I never could have imagined that I would be at peace again. Here in this monastery, it dawns on me that I may just be finding my way.

Day 65

Its the early morning and I’m waiting for the sun to rise and melt the ice on the road. Today I ride my final kilometres of this Camino. I expect to bear witness to the Compostela this evening. Bittersweet emotions overcome me as one chapter comes to an end and another begins.

I will update you all on my next chapter of this journey. Love and life.

item.title: In Case of Emergency
item.description: A reminder of the truth for when the mind sinks into darkness.
item.content:encoded:
I know life seems harder right now. Everything seems pointless, even reading this seems pointless. Just remember you have been here before. Every time you beat it, you are a warrior. It’s times like these when you get to prove your merits. Now is when you earn your colours.

You are a miracle and you deserve love. Love yourself first, be kind.

Top Ten Steps to Find your Way

  1. Everything seems worse now, remind yourself what is good.
  2. Don’t listen to any negativity, if it’s not positive then shut it up.
  3. Give yourself a little time to rest. Slow down. Use this time to reinforce positive thinking.
  4. Read your goals, remember your focus.
  5. Stop thinking so far ahead, a journey of a 1000 miles starts with a single step.
  6. Take the time to take action in the areas you have been neglecting. Small steps.
  7. Meditate on love. You too deserve love.
  8. Reminisce about the good times, listen to old songs, look at old photos. Saudade. Without sadness, there can be no joy.
  9. Inspect your diet, get eating healthy.
  10. Start exercising. Small steps.

Love yourself first, and all others after.
